title: Weingart
description: A song credit set like a forme of hand-set metal type: three lines of title on a flush-left margin, a process-red running time printed underneath, brass rule, the writer's credit set plain on the margin and on the red's own baseline, so the foot of the forme is one line from the credit to the figure, and a colophon hung flush left on the figure's edge from the cap line of the title, so at rest the forme has two verticals, one shared foot and no stair anywhere. Every line is a row of single sorts, and every line's first sort is locked to the margin. Push a line and it hinges there like a lever, a step at a time: the far letter drops first, then the middle tips, and only a long pull breaks the word into a full staircase. Every sort drops straight down, its own piece of lead, so a word keeps its shape while its baseline breaks, and the Swiss margin it starts from never moves. The sorts are solid and stay in contact the way real lead does: a line that comes down onto the next one shoves the letters it lands on a step, and that line bends to them from the margin and, past that knee, takes on the riser of the line that hit it, sort for sort, and so on down the forme, each sort seating with its own knock, left to right, until the run locks. No sort ever hangs more than its own body below the one before it, and every riser, type or brass, is a whole number of the rule's own body, so a full push ends with the three title lines as parallel stairs of one pitch. The brass prints only its fine face: where the rule breaks, its separate lengths simply sit at their own depths, ends butted, as broken lead does in a forme. The rule's last piece, cut to the figure's measure, holds over the red's cap line as a head rule while the run behind it steps, and only when the push reaches the red's feet does it drop in one knock across them. There the black overprints the red, and the two inks make a third, darker one, and the forme locks on one bottom line: credit at the margin, figure at the right, brass seated across its feet.
intent: After Wolfgang Weingart's Basel letterpress experiments and his stepped Typografische Monatsblätter covers (1972–73): Swiss order broken from inside the system, using the real constraints of a press, quantised steps, letterspacing and overprinting, to make new rhythm. https://neugraphic.com/weingart/weingart-text2.html
